news.headline: Why This One Company Is So Good At Making Everything
news.summary: Xiaomi competes in more than 200 product categories, from smartphones and rice cookers to smart toilets and electric cars. SharkNinja’s roughly 40 categories look small next to that, so how does one company pull it off? Learn the smartest moves from nine iconic brands: https://clickhubspot.com/u8hf In 2011, Xiaomi launched its first phone at about $300, undercutting the big brands. Founder Lei Jun never wanted to stop at phones, though. He wanted Xiaomi in every room of your house, and found a creative way to get there. In 2014, Xiaomi put $3 million into a startup called Roborock before that startup had shipped a single product. Roborock’s first robot vacuum launched under Xiaomi’s name. When Roborock went public at a $4.7 billion valuation Xiaomi kept a stake worth nearly a quarter of the company. The hit looks small for now, since satellite signals struggle to reach phones indoors, but SpaceX’s planned rooftop micro cell towers aim at that gap.
